# MTSQL-R1: Towards Long-Horizon Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL via Agentic Training

## Research question

Conversational SQL generation can drop prior constraints or misinterpret references even when its output executes successfully.

## Method

MTSQL-R1 learns a propose–execute–verify–correct loop with database feedback and retrieval of earlier SQL, parsed clauses and results. Self-generated trajectories filtered against gold SQL initialize supervised training, followed by curriculum GRPO with outcome and action-specific rewards. Memory verification is a model judgment prompted with historical evidence.

## Evaluation

CoSQL and SParC experiments compare execution match and EM, with Qwen3-1.7B/4B and a Llama3.2-3B extension. Main evaluation uses gold previous SQL; a separate CoSQL experiment uses predicted history. Ablations remove execution or memory checks. Additional tests cover dataset transfer, single-turn data and generation latency; GPT-5 labels coherence-error categories.

## What the results support

The reported 4B CoSQL execution score falls from 79.9 to 77.8 without memory verification and to 74.6 without execution. With predicted history, the full model scores 76.5 versus 71.2 for direct RL. Aggregation-drift errors remain, and the full loop uses more tokens and time.

## Limits and qualifications

Reference-based rewards and learned checks do not certify intended semantics. The null-result reward category is not an answerability label; correct empty answers are not separately evaluated. Coherence-error analysis uses a gold-aware model judge. The released EM and verification-tag handling differ from the paper description, limiting exact reproducibility from this snapshot. No user clarification, refusal policy or industrial-scale schema study is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adjacent support for checking conversational constraints during SQL generation, with explicit evidence about the dependence on prior SQL quality. It does not establish preservation of user-confirmed intent or resolution of genuine ambiguity.
